subject: PayGrid: Follow-up & next steps — model fit / parity review
messages:
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sam Patel <sam.patel@paygrid.com>
Cc: Asha Narayan <asha@paygrid.com>
Date: Thu, 10 Dec 2026 15:22:00 -0800
Subject: PayGrid: Follow-up & next steps — model fit / parity review

Hi Sam —

Thanks for taking time today — appreciated the context on PayGrid's billing QPS, latency targets, and how you measure downstream accuracy for invoice classification. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can move toward a focused model-fit eval: 

Recap from call:
- Goal: determine whether an open-model stack can meet PayGrid's parity/acceptance thresholds vs your current proprietary baseline for key invoice-classification intents.
- Key constraints: end-to-end latency target ~<400ms p95 for in-line flows, acceptable accuracy drop <= ~3% absolute from baseline on critical labels, and bounded hallucination rate for vendor IDs.
- Data: you can share a 1k-sample de-identified prompt set we can run for an initial benchmark.

Proposed next steps: 
1) Sam/PayGrid: share the de-identified prompt set + any label mapping/acceptance criteria (if you have a one-pager) — target: EOD Mon (12/13).
2) Redwood (Marissa + Aditya): run a 1k model-fit eval across 3 recommended open/proprietary-compatible variants, return a short parity summary + recommended next steps within 3 business days of receiving the sample.
3) Joint sync: 30-min recap to review results + alignment on acceptance thresholds — propose Thurs 12/16 or Fri 12/17.

What we need from you to be most effective:
- The de-identified prompt set (1k ideally, csv or jsonl)
- Any explicit acceptance thresholds or examples of failure modes you want us to prioritize
- Callouts on latency SLOs and preferred regions (us-east/us-west)

I attached a short acceptance-criteria template that helps us capture thresholds (see attached: paygrid-acceptance-criteria.pdf).

If that timeline looks good I’ll kick this off internally and loop in the eval owner (Marissa) to run the artifacts.

Thanks —
Lauren Bishop
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference
lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com
Redwood Inference

[attachment: paygrid-acceptance-criteria.pdf (PDF, 1 page)]

From: Sam Patel <sam.patel@paygrid.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Asha Narayan <asha@paygrid.com>
Date: Fri, 11 Dec 2026 09:10:00 -0800
Subject: Re: PayGrid: Follow-up & next steps — model fit / parity review

Thanks Lauren —

Appreciate the clear recap. We can share a de-identified 1k prompt set by EOD Monday (12/13). Attaching our internal acceptance thresholds (high-level) for your reference. A couple of questions from my side before you run the eval: 

- Baseline: our current baseline is a licensed proprietary model (vendor-provided) tuned on our ledger data — we can share aggregate metrics but not the model itself. We care about two things: matching accuracy on invoice type + vendor-id extraction and keeping false positives on vendor-id extraction below 1.5%.
- Can Redwood run both label-level accuracy and a small hallucination audit? Also need to understand expected latency in a cloud-hosted Redwood-hosted config vs private deployment.

Open to the 12/16 or 12/17 recap — prefer 12/16 in the morning PT.

Attachments: paygrid-acceptance-criteria.pdf (the file has the thresholds and a short glossary).

Best,
Sam
Sam Patel
VP Product, PayGrid
sam.patel@paygrid.com

Subject: Fwd: PayGrid: Follow-up & next steps — model fit / parity review

Marissa / Aditya —

Fwd'ing PayGrid's acceptance criteria and the ask. High priority — Sam wants a 1k-run and a short parity summary (label-level accuracy + hallucination audit) by ~3 business days after we receive the data. Please confirm feasibility and owners.

What I need from you:
- Marissa: lead the eval. Run the 1k sample across the following recommended candidates (unless you have better suggestions):
  * redwood-rlm-7b-8bit (open quantized variant)
  * meta-llama2-13b-instruct-8bit
  * mistral-7b-instruct-8k-quant
  Also include a tuned small-proprietary-compatible variant if we have an internal comparator.
- Deliverables: per-model CSV with predictions, label-level precision/recall/F1, hallucination audit (sampled 50 errors, short notes), latency p95 numbers (us-east).
- Aditya: provide cost estimate (per-1k-run token counts, expected steady-state per-token cost and anticipated infra config: hosted vs dedicated) and a short note on deployment tradeoffs for PayGrid (latency vs cost).

Timeline: assume we get PayGrid's 1k set Mon 12/13 — can you have an initial summary (slides + raw CSVs + eval report) by Thu 12/16 10:00 PT? Sam asked for morning that day. If that's tight, call out what you need.

I attached the acceptance criteria PDF the customer sent.

Thanks —
Lauren

[Forwarded attachment: paygrid-acceptance-criteria.pdf]

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sat, 12 Dec 2026 08:30:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Fwd: PayGrid: Follow-up & next steps — model fit / parity review

Lauren / Aditya —

I can take the eval. Quick notes and plan so expectations are clear: 

Planned candidate models (initial run):
- redwood-rlm-7b-8bit (our quantized RL-trained 7B) — expect best cost/latency balance.
- meta-llama2-13b-instruct-8bit — stronger instruction-following, higher inference cost.
- mistral-7b-instruct-8k-quant — good for longer context, competitive accuracy.
- internal small-tuned comparator (if we can surface a tuned checkpoint quickly) — will include if available.

Evaluation metrics and acceptance thresholds we’ll report:
- Label-level precision/recall/F1 (primary acceptance: <= 3% absolute drop from PayGrid baseline on critical labels).
- Hallucination audit: sampled 50 error cases with short notes; target false-positive rate for vendor-id < 1.5%.
- Latency: p50/p95 for in-region (us-east) hosted config; target p95 < 400ms for the inline path.
- Cost: per-1k sample inference token counts and estimated hosted cost.

Deliverables: 
- redwood-paygrid-eval-report.pdf (short narrative + recommendations)
- per-model csv files with predictions and error tags
- prompt set + canonical prompt template used for test runs (jsonl)

Links / references:
- Eval folder (drive): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-paygrid-evals
- Internal eval dashboard (read-only): https://redwood-internal/reports/paygrid-eval-dashboard

Acceptance thresholds (proposed):
- Critical label F1 >= baseline_F1 - 0.03 (absolute)
- Vendor-id false positive rate <= 1.5%
- Latency p95 (us-east) <= 400ms

I'll run the 1k job as soon as Sam drops the data (EOD 12/13) — preliminary artifacts will be in the drive + I’ll attach the short PDF report. If Aditya can provide expected per-token accounting I’ll include that in the recommendations slide.

Marissa
Senior ML Engineer, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com
